summary: Kashi Prasad Jayaswal (1881–1937) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Allahabad, Jesus College, Oxford (M.A. ~1906–1909), and Lincoln's Inn. He served as Tagore Professor of Law at Calcutta (1917) and president of the Numismatic Society of India.

Kashinath Narayan Dikshit (1889–1944) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, as Officiating Government Epigraphist for India (attested 1931), and as Deputy Director-General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India (1937–1944).

Kashinath Trimbak Telang (1850–1893) was an Indologist. He studied at Elphinstone College and Mumbai under Narayan Mahadev Parmanand, later serving as Senior Dakshina Fellow at Elphinstone, vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1892–1893), and President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar (1890–1976) worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat Arts & Science College (~1914–1945) and as Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1945–1976).

Kate Crosby is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She held positions at St Peter's College, Oxford (attested 1996), Cardiff University (attested 2002), the Buddhist Institute (2003), and the Seiyu Kiriyama post in Buddhist Studies at SOAS.

Kate Wharton is a scholar in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London in 2008 and held a post at Birkbeck, University of London (attested 2010).
Katharina Sabernig is a tibetology and history/archaeology scholar. She completed her PhD at the University of Vienna in 2017 and held a post at the Medical University of Vienna.
Katherine Anne Narraway works in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her Master of Arts degree at McGill University, where she studied under MA supervisor G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2008).

Katherine Anne Paul works in tibetology, history/archaeology, and Indology. She completed doctoral research under Gudrun Bühnemann and studied with teachers including Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

Katherine Janiec Jones specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied at Davidson College and earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Paul J. Griffiths, also studying under William K. Mahony and Karl A. Plank.

Katherine K. Young (born 1944) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She earned an M.A. from the University of Chicago and a Ph.D. from McGill University, where she became a professor around 1978.

Kathleen D. Morrison (born 1963) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Notre Dame, New Mexico, and UC Berkeley. She was Assistant Professor of Anthropology at Northwestern (~1993–1995) and joined the University of Pennsylvania (~2017).

Kathleen Kenyon (1906–1978) was an archaeologist. She studied at St Paul's Girls' School and Somerville College, Oxford. Her career included posts at the University of London (~1935–1962), UCL Institute of Archaeology (1948–1962), and St Hugh's College (1962–1973).

Kathleen M. Erndl (1954–2017) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. She held posts at DePauw, Wisconsin-Madison, and Lewis & Clark (~1987–1993) before serving as Associate Professor of Religion at Florida State University (~1993–2017).

Kathleen Marie Higgins (born 1954) is a philosophy scholar. Appointed Professor of Philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin around 1986, she has also held visiting posts at the Bellagio Center (1993), Australian National University (1997), and Canberra School of Music (1997).

Kathleen McDonald (born 1952) is an author and scholar in Buddhist studies and tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers including Tenzin Gyatso, Yeshe Thubten, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche (attested 2010).
Kathrin Holz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and held a research affiliation post at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Kathryn H. Selig Brown specializes in tibetology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Walter M. Spink at the University of Michigan, completing her Doctor of Philosophy degree in 2000.
Kathryn R. Blackstone is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She has held posts at the University of Manitoba (attested 1999) and Victoria University of Wellington.

Katia Buffetrille (born 1948) specializes in tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Paris Nanterre University under Alexander W. Macdonald, and held posts at EPHE (~1998), CRCAO (attested 2003), and as editor of Études mongoles, sibériennes, centrasiatiques et tibétaines.
